title: Fletcher Henderson stand-in, the Roseland matinee and Big Green
summary: Cootie went on the road with Fletcher Henderson, missed the Roseland matinee believing the stand-in was over, and Bobby Stark protected him from Big Green.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And you went out on the road with him for a week.
No. He had to get permission from Chick for me to go with him.
Yeah.

And I went out maybe about two or three weeks, with Fletcher. Then we came back to New York. We were to open up at Roseland for a Sunday matinee. So I thought -- I was offended when we got back to New York, so I don't go and open up. I don't go down there.
Well, why? Did you think Pop Smith had come back?
No. Because the arrangement was that I was only to go on the road with him until he come back.
Until Pops came back.
No. Until the band came back.
Oh. Until the band came back.
And I will, you know --
Yeah.
That was the agreement between him and Chick.
Yeah.

And so I don't go and make the matinee. So they can't start playing nothing. So they got somebody to come up there and get me. Oh, I'm telling you. And I rushed myself and got on down there. And when I did get there and got on the bandstand, I said -- and then Big Green was behind
me. Big Greene was sitting up there. He scared me to death. He said, "I'm going to kill you when you get off there." "When you get off this bandstand, you little so and so, I'm going to kill you."
(Laughter)
So I'm shaking like a leaf.
(Laughter)
You really think -- was he really serious?
Yeah.
He really was mad.
Yeah. And so we kept on playing and kept on playing. So Bobby Stark says, "Hey, you big so and so, leave that boy alone. Don't you bother that boy. Shut up and leave that boy alone." And he shut up.
(Laughter)
Little Bobby done talked to him like that, I won't be afraid of him no more.
(Laughter)
So I got the fear out of me, and I went on playing then. And I wasn't afraid of him no more.
How funny.
So when he come off the bandstand, he don't said a word to me.
No kidding?
Uh-uh.
Bobby knew you were scared, then?
Yeah. I'm sitting right next to Bobby, so Bobby knows I'm afraid.
Well, isn't that funny. Well, after all, I mean -- well, maybe they didn't know that that was the arrangement.
No. They didn't know that.
Yeah.
And maybe Fletcher had forgot about it.
Yeah. Yeah. Probably, because he didn't think too much
Yeah.
Yeah.
And of course, it was in my mind, so when I went on the road, I was to go out there for two or three weeks. Whatever period of time. When I got back, that was the end of it.
Yeah.
And so ain't nobody said nothing to me, you know, so I thought I was finished, you know?
Well, so then Fletcher had to get back in touch with Chick, then.
Yeah.
I mean, by then -- by now it's established
Yeah. So I stayed in the band.
What did Chick have to say about that? Tell you he wouldn't stand in your way or something?
No. I used to give him money when I come in. He wasn't working then.
Yeah.
So -- so Johnny Hodges told Duke about me.
